title: Path-aware lint sharding with dynamic cache warming and dep-gate integration
author: Maya Chen
commits: introduce path-aware shard mapper for lint (tools/ci/path_shard_mapper.py)
add cache-warm action and helper script (.github/actions/cache-warm + scripts/ci/cache-warm.sh)
wire path-aware lint into workflow and fast-feedback lanes (.github/workflows/lint.yml, .github/workflows/fast-feedback.yml)
bump composite-action versions and update lockfile (package-lock.json)
fix tests and adjust shard fallback logic after review
description:
Context and motivation: Our lint stage is a significant part of CI latency and runner cost for PRs that touch many packages. Historically we used static shard mapping which runs wide for monorepo-wide changes and conservatively for small PRs. This PR implements a path-aware lint sharding mapper plus a lightweight cache-warming step to (1) reduce unnecessary shard runs on small CLs, (2) ensure shards hit warmed caches for faster cold-starts, and (3) integrate with the dependency gate so dependency bumps that touch lots of files still run the proper shards.

What changed (single-string summary): Added a small Python shard mapper that maps changed paths to lint shards using repository topology heuristics, introduced a reusable cache-warm action and a shell helper to prime runner caches when a shard is scheduled, updated lint and fast-feedback workflows to call the mapper and conditionally skip or target shards, bumped composite action versions and updated package-lock.json, and added documentation and rollout/rollback guidance.

Implementation notes: The shard mapper (tools/ci/path_shard_mapper.py) computes a set of affected packages using repository package manifests and a configurable path=>shard mapping table. It falls back to the full lint set if touched paths are ambiguous (e.g., build system changes). The mapper emits a JSON-friendly string list used by GitHub Actions matrix.include. The cache-warm action is a tiny composite that runs in a single short job to pre-fetch common caches (node_modules tarballs, wheel caches, wheelhouse) for the targeted shard. The workflows were refactored so that: (a) staged fast-feedback lane runs the path-aware partial shard set for quick signal, (b) the full lint stage still runs on main and on PRs that touch infra files, and (c) an env var CI_FORCE_FULL_LINT allows emergency overrides.

Testing and CI: New unit tests for path_shard_mapper are included and run in the lint job. End-to-end validation performed on a sample set of 42 historical PRs: median lint job time reduced ~38% and runner minutes reduced ~29% for small PRs. Initial CI run flagged a flaky cache-warm timeout when runner image pull was slow; adjusted timeout and added exponential retry. Final CI status: passing checks (lint, unit, e2e-sim).

Rollout plan: Feature guarded behind a repo-level flag. Gradual rollout to all repos in three waves (team-owned -> cross-team -> global) over two weeks. Monitoring: added metric ci.path_shard_skipped_count and ci.cache_warm_latency to the CI dashboard; alerts if skipped shard rate drops below threshold (indicating mapper regressions).

Rollback: If the mapper causes unexpected skips we can set CI_FORCE_FULL_LINT=1 in the repo settings or revert the workflow changes.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement shard mapper and tests
- [x] Add cache-warm action and retries
- [x] Wire into workflows and fast-feedback lane
- [x] Update docs/CI runbook
- [x] Run historical simulation and e2e smoke runs
- [x] Obtain approvals from infra and SRE leads

References: Linear ENG-1129 tracks mapper work; ENG-2347 tracks cache warm and rollout. Related prior work: perf sharding prototypes in ENG-980.
review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Nice approach — the heuristic table is straightforward. Two requests: add a unit test that simulates a root-level buildfile change (should fallback to full run), and add a comment explaining the fallback threshold (why 3 packages?).
Maya Chen (author): Added test simulating root-level buildfile and increased comment in mapper; fallback threshold is now configurable via env var and documented in README.
Priya Nair: CI run looks good. One nit: cache-warm action retries should back off more aggressively for slower registries. Can we add jitter?
Maya Chen (author): Implemented exponential backoff with jitter in scripts/ci/cache-warm.sh — pushed change and retriggered CI.
Samir Patel: Verified simulator results vs historical PR subset. Approve after green CI and a quick canary on infra-team repos.
CI Bot: initial lint job failed on cache-warm timeout (image pull). Rerun returned green after timeout bump and retry logic.
Release Manager (automated): Merged via squash after approvals and passing CI.
release_notes: Introduce path-aware lint sharding and lightweight cache warming to reduce CI latency and runner cost for small PRs. Guarded rollout and can be disabled via CI_FORCE_FULL_LINT. Monitoring and alerts added for shard skipping and cache warm latency.
